## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D1 (a, foundations). This is audit backlog UX-13 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Every form and table, all roles; shown first in /__ui. The platform console inherits it.
Findings and reviewers: F-20, F-33, F-44, F-24 (labels) · reviewers C-01, C-13, C-22, B-20, A-17.
Rationale: The library default (36 px) contradicts the house 44 px rule, so 164 call sites patch it and a missed patch gives a small control (seen in the platform console). Four scrollable tables have no label, so keyboard users cannot name or scroll them. Switches are 32 by 18 px. This is one of the three system changes the arbitration allows before the pilot.
Proposed UX behaviour: In packages/ui: Input, SelectTrigger and Textarea default to 44 px; select options are 44 px on a coarse pointer; Table's label prop becomes required in TypeScript, and the four tables without one (day sheet, merge review, growth card, timeline) get a translated label in the same change; Switch keeps its track size and gains a 44 by 44 px hit area by padding. A ChoiceRow helper makes the whole row the target of a native radio or checkbox. The gallery shows each control at default size with its measured height, in English and Arabic. The call-site patches stay in place in this ticket (they are now redundant, not wrong) and are deleted by the codemod ticket that follows.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 4 (Density) and section 7 (Before the pilot).
Components and tokens affected: input.tsx, select.tsx, textarea.tsx, table.tsx, switch.tsx; new ChoiceRow; gallery entries. No token change.
Front end and back end split: Front end only (packages/ui, four table labels with i18n keys in en, hi and ar).
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the lint and ratchet ticket (D0). File ownership in wave D1a: this ticket owns the five control files above and nothing in tokens or styles.css.
Clinical sign-off: Not required. The device check (question 20 of the validation plan) confirms mouse or touch at the pilot desk; the default is safe for both.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. Visible change only where a control was never patched.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Deleting the call-site patches (the codemod ticket, which merges alone). (2) Applying ChoiceRow to the 26 native radios and checkboxes in features, and making name-link rows one target (second part of the codemod ticket). (3) Compact density (after the pilot, with the table ticket).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given the /__ui gallery, when Input, Select trigger and Textarea render with no class added, then each is at least 44 px tall in English and in Arabic
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the screens that already patched their controls to 44 px, when screenshots before and after are compared, then no control changed size
- [ ] **AC3.** Given the call sites that had no patch, when the change is reviewed, then the pull request lists each one and each now measures 44 px, including the platform console invite form
- [ ] **AC4.** Given any Table in web/clinic or web/platform-admin, when it is used without a label, then TypeScript fails the build, and the four tables that lacked one announce a translated label to a screen reader
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a Switch on a 1024 px touch viewport, when its hit area is measured, then it is at least 44 by 44 px and the visible track is unchanged
- [ ] **AC6.** Given the gallery page in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation and the controls mirror in right-to-left

## Test notes

- Vitest: default heights and the required label (type test).
- Playwright (new step in the gallery spec, or tests/e2e/page-layout.spec.ts): on /__ui at 1024 touch, no library control is under 44 px; axe clean in en and ar.
- Existing suites stay green: no selector depends on control height.

## Notes / open questions

- Regression risk: low.
